liveClass.title: Aynı cümle, beş ses
liveClass.goal: Öğretmen sade bir paragraf verir (örneğin bir şehirde yaşanan büyük bir fırtına). Gruplar paragrafı önce bir roman sahnesi (yer devrikliği, öne alma), sonra bir anma konuşması (Such was ..., Never before ..., Come what may) olarak yeniden yazar ve okur. Sınıf her versiyonda hangi yapının en etkili olduğunu tartışır ve aşırı kullanımın etkisini değerlendirir.

lessons.title: Öne alma (fronting)
lessons.goal: Sıfat, zarf ya da nesneyi cümle başına alarak (Tired as she was, Strange though it may seem, This I cannot accept) vurgu ve üslup katabilirim.

discover.title: Bir romandan
discover.body: Exhausted as she was, Nehir refused to stop. The last train had long gone, and the city was silent. Strange though it may seem, she felt no fear, only a quiet determination. The letter she had promised to deliver was still in her coat pocket. That letter she would deliver, whatever it cost. Much as she wanted to sleep, she knew that by morning it would be too late. So she walked on, through the empty streets, towards the old harbour.

options: It would be too late to deliver the letter.
She had to catch a train.
questions.explanation: "by morning it would be too late"

learn.explanation:
**Öne alma (fronting),** normalde cümlenin sonunda olan bir öğeyi başa taşıyarak **vurgu** ya da **bağlam** oluşturmaktır.

**1. Sıfat / zarf + as / though + özne + fiil (= Although ...):**

| Normal | Öne alınmış |
|---|---|
| Although she was exhausted, ... | **Exhausted as / though she was**, ... |
| Although it may seem strange, ... | **Strange though / as it may seem**, ... |
| Although he tried hard, ... | **Hard as he tried**, ... |
| Although I like him a lot, ... | **Much as I like him**, ... |

**Dikkat:**

- Öne alınan sıfattan önce **a / an** kullanılmaz: ✓ *Brilliant scientist though he was*.
- Bu yapıda **as**, "çünkü" değil **"-e rağmen"** anlamındadır!
- *Much as* özellikle *like, love, admire, want, hate* ile kullanılır.

**2. Nesneyi öne alma (object fronting):** Konuşmada ve edebiyatta güçlü vurgu ya da karşıtlık için.

- ***That letter** she would deliver, whatever it cost.*
- ***This** I cannot accept.*
- ***What he did next**, nobody could have predicted.*
- *Some of the songs I loved; **others** I couldn't stand.*

**3. Tamamlayıcıyı öne alma:**

- ***Gone** are the days when ...* (... günler geride kaldı)
- ***Equally important** is the question of cost.*
- ***More worrying** is the lack of evidence.*

Bu son yapılarda **özne ile fiil yer değiştirir** (devrik).

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede öğe sırası esnektir ve vurgulanan öğe genellikle yüklemin hemen önüne konur ("O mektubu teslim edecekti" / "Teslim edecekti o mektubu"). İngilizcede ise öğe sırası katıdır; bu yüzden öne alma güçlü ve dikkat çekici bir üslup tercihidir. Türk öğrencilerin en sık karıştırdığı nokta, "Tired as she was" yapısındaki "as"in "çünkü" değil "-e rağmen" anlamına gelmesidir. Türkçedeki "Ne kadar yorgun olsa da" yapısıyla eşleştirin.

task.prompt: Zor bir dönemde azimle bir şey başardığınız bir deneyimi (sınav, spor, iş, taşınma) kısa ve etkileyici bir hikâye olarak anlatın (1 dakika). En az 3 öne alma yapısı kullanın: Tired / Hard / Much as ..., Strange though it may seem, Gone are the days ..., That I would never forget, More surprising was ...
task.modelAnswer: Three years ago, I decided to run my first half-marathon. Busy as I was with work, I trained every morning at six. Hard as I tried, I couldn't get faster than twelve kilometres an hour, and I nearly gave up. Strange though it may seem, it was a stranger who changed everything. An older runner saw me struggling one day and gave me a simple tip about breathing. That advice I will never forget. On race day, I finished in just under two hours. More surprising than my time was how happy I felt. Gone are the days when I thought I wasn't a sporty person.

lessons.title: Yer ve yön devrikliği
lessons.goal: Edebi ve betimleyici metinlerde yer, yön ve hareket bildiren ifadelerle devrik yapıyı (In the corner stood a piano / Down came the rain / Here comes the bus) anlayıp kullanabilirim.

discover.title: Bir öyküden
discover.body: At the end of the narrow street stood an old stone house. Above the door hung a rusty lantern, swinging gently in the wind. Inside, the air was cold. In the corner sat an old man, wrapped in a blanket, staring at the fire. On the table lay a pile of yellowed letters. Suddenly, there was a crash of thunder, and down came the rain. The door flew open, and in rushed a young woman, soaking wet. "There you are!" said the old man. "I've been waiting for you."

questions.explanation: "On the table lay a pile of yellowed letters."

questions.explanation: "in rushed a young woman, soaking wet"

learn.explanation:
**Yer / yön devrikliği (locative inversion),** edebi ve betimleyici metinlerde, okuyucunun dikkatini önce **mekâna**, sonra **özneye** çekmek için kullanılır.

**Yapı:** Yer / yön ifadesi + **fiil** + özne

**1. Yer ifadeleriyle (durum fiilleri: stand, sit, lie, hang, live):**

| Normal | Devrik |
|---|---|
| An old house stood at the end of the street. | **At the end of the street stood** an old house. |
| A lantern hung above the door. | **Above the door hung** a lantern. |
| A pile of letters lay on the table. | **On the table lay** a pile of letters. |

**2. Yön zarflarıyla (hareket fiilleri: come, go, run, fly, rush):**

| Normal | Devrik |
|---|---|
| The rain came down. | **Down came** the rain. |
| A young woman rushed in. | **In rushed** a young woman. |
| The balloon went up. | **Up went** the balloon. |

**3. Here / There ile (konuşmada çok yaygın):**

- ***Here comes** the bus!*
- ***There goes** my last chance.*
- ***Here's** your coffee.*

**Önemli kural: Özne zamir ise devrik yapılmaz!**

| İsim özne | Zamir özne |
|---|---|
| ✓ *Here comes **the bus**.* | ✓ *Here **it comes**.* (✗ *Here comes it.*) |
| ✓ *Down came **the rain**.* | ✓ *Down **it came**.* |
| ✓ *There goes **Ali**.* | ✓ *There **he goes**.* |

**Not:** Bu yapı genellikle yardımcı fiil olmadan, **basit geçmiş** ya da **geniş zamanla** kullanılır.

Ancak iki noktaya dikkat edin: (1) İngilizcede bu yapı edebi ve betimleyicidir; günlük yazışmalarda kullanılmaz ("Here comes the bus" gibi kalıplar hariç). (2) Özne zamir olduğunda devrik yapılmaz: "Here it comes", ✗ "Here comes it".

task.prompt: Gözlerinizi kapatın ve çok sevdiğiniz bir yeri (çocukluk eviniz, bir kafe, bir köy meydanı) hayal edin. Bu yeri bir romanın açılış sahnesi gibi betimleyin (1 dakika). En az 4 yer devrikliği (In the corner stood ..., On the wall hung ..., Above the door ...) ve en az 1 yön devrikliği (In came ..., Out ran ..., Down came ...) kullanın.
task.modelAnswer: At the end of a narrow street in my grandparents' village stood a small white house. Above the blue door hung a basket of red geraniums. Inside, the kitchen smelled of fresh bread. In the corner stood an old wooden cupboard, full of my grandmother's jars of jam. On the wall hung a black-and-white photograph of my grandparents on their wedding day. Every evening at six, in came my grandfather from the fields, with mud on his boots and a huge smile on his face. And out ran all of us children to greet him.

lessons.title: İleri vurgu yapıları
lessons.goal: Such was ..., So great was ..., Nowhere ..., Not once ..., On no account ..., In no way ... gibi ileri devrik vurgu yapılarını resmî konuşma ve yazıda kullanabilirim.

discover.title: Bir anma konuşmasından
discover.body: Such was her dedication to her students that she rarely left the school before eight in the evening. So great was her influence that many of them became teachers themselves. Not once in forty years did she miss a day of work. Nowhere else have I met a person so generous with her time. On no account would she accept praise; she always insisted that the credit belonged to her students. In no way can words express how much we will miss her.

questions.prompt: How long did the teacher work?
How did she react to praise?
questions.explanation: "On no account would she accept praise"

learn.explanation:
C1 Ünite 1'de *Never, Rarely, Not only, No sooner, Little did* gibi devrik yapıları gördük. C2'de daha ileri ve resmî yapılara geçiyoruz.

**1. Such was / were + isim + that ...:** (O kadar ... idi ki)

| Normal | Devrik |
|---|---|
| Her dedication was so great that ... | **Such was her dedication that** ... |
| The crowds were so large that ... | **Such were the crowds that** ... |

**2. So + sıfat + was / were + özne + that ...:**

| Normal | Devrik |
|---|---|
| The demand was so great that ... | **So great was the demand that** ... |
| He was so tired that ... | **So tired was he that** ... |

**3. Olumsuz ve kısıtlayıcı ifadelerle devrik yapı:**

| İfade | Örnek |
|---|---|
| **Nowhere** | **Nowhere** else **have I** met such a person. |
| **Not once** | **Not once did** she complain. |
| **On no account** | **On no account should** you leave. |
| **In no way** | **In no way can** words express ... |
| **At no time** | **At no time was** the public in danger. |
| **Under no circumstances** | **Under no circumstances will** we accept late work. |
| **Only then** | **Only then did** I understand. |
| **Not a single ...** | **Not a single word did** he say. |

**Kural:** Bu ifadelerden sonra soru düzeni gelir: **yardımcı fiil + özne + ana fiil**. Yardımcı fiil yoksa **do / does / did** eklenir.

**Kullanım:** Resmî konuşma, anma, haber, edebi metin. Günlük konuşmada **abartılı** gelir.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede vurgu genellikle "o kadar ... ki", "hiçbir surette", "bir kez bile" gibi ifadelerle ve tonlamayla yapılır, cümle yapısı değişmez. İngilizcede ise bu ifadeler başa geldiğinde soru düzeni zorunludur. Türk öğrencilerin sık yaptığı hata, devrik yapıyı unutmaktır: ✗ "Not once she complained." ✓ "Not once did she complain." Ayrıca "Such was" ile "So + sıfat + was" yapısını karıştırmayın: Such + isim, So + sıfat.

task.prompt: Hayatınızda önemli bir yeri olan bir kişiyi (öğretmen, aile büyüğü, bir lider) onurlandıran kısa bir resmî konuşma yapın (1 dakika). En az 5 ileri vurgu yapısı kullanın: Such was ..., So great / generous was ..., Not once did ..., Nowhere else have I ..., In no way can ..., Only then did I ..., At no time ...
task.modelAnswer: Today, I would like to pay tribute to my grandfather, who passed away last year. Such was his kindness that our door was always open to neighbours in need. So generous was he that he often gave away more than he could afford. Not once did I hear him speak badly of anyone. Nowhere else have I met a person who listened so patiently. When I was young, I didn't understand his quiet strength. Only later did I realise how much he had taught me. In no way can these few words do justice to the man he was, but I hope they remind us of how he lived.

lessons.title: Şart devrikliği ve kalıplaşmış dilek kipi
lessons.goal: Were it not for / Had it not been for gibi şart devriklikleri ve Be that as it may, Come what may, Suffice it to say, Far be it from me gibi kalıplaşmış dilek kipi (subjunctive) ifadelerini yerinde kullanabilirim.

discover.title: Bir yöneticinin mektubundan
discover.body:
Dear team,

Were it not for your hard work this year, we would not be celebrating our best results in a decade. Had it not been for your patience during the difficult spring months, many of our clients would have left us.

I am aware that some of you have concerns about the planned reorganisation. Be that as it may, I believe it is the right decision for the company's future. Far be it from me to pretend that change is easy, but I am confident that, come what may, we will face it together.

Suffice it to say that I am extremely proud of what we have achieved. If need be, I will meet each of you individually to discuss your concerns.

With warm regards,
Defne Arslan, Managing Director

questions.prompt: Why does the director thank the team?
options: For the best results in a decade

questions.prompt: What does the director offer to do?
options: Meet each person individually if necessary
questions.explanation: "If need be, I will meet each of you individually"

learn.explanation:
**1. Were it not for / Had it not been for (= If it weren't for / If it hadn't been for):**

| Normal | Devrik (resmî) | Zaman |
|---|---|---|
| If it weren't for your help, I would fail. | **Were it not for** your help, I would fail. | şimdi |
| If it hadn't been for the rain, we would have won. | **Had it not been for** the rain, we would have won. | geçmiş |
| If it hadn't been for you, I would be lost now. | **Had it not been for** you, I would be lost now. | karışık |

**Not:** *But for* (C1 Ünite 3) de aynı anlamdadır ve daha kısadır: *But for your help, ...*

**2. Kalıplaşmış dilek kipi (formulaic subjunctive):** Fiilin yalın hali (*be, come, suffice*) kullanılan, eski İngilizceden kalma sabit ifadeler.

| İfade | Anlam | Örnek |
|---|---|---|
| **Be that as it may, ...** | Her ne olursa olsun, yine de | **Be that as it may**, we must decide today. |
| **Come what may, ...** | Ne olursa olsun | **Come what may**, I'll support you. |
| **Suffice it to say (that) ...** | Şu kadarını söyleyeyim ki | **Suffice it to say** he wasn't happy. |
| **Far be it from me to ...** | -mek bana düşmez ama | **Far be it from me to** criticise, but ... |
| **If need be, ...** | Gerekirse | I'll stay late **if need be**. |
| **So be it.** | Öyle olsun. | If that's what you want, **so be it**. |
| **God / Heaven forbid!** | Allah korusun! | **Heaven forbid** anything should go wrong. |
| **Long live ...!** | Çok yaşa ...! | **Long live** the king! |

**Not:** *Far be it from me to ...* genellikle tam da "bana düşmez" dediğiniz şeyi yapacağınızı gösterir (ironik): *Far be it from me to tell you what to do, but ...*

**3. Önceden gördüğümüz dilek kipi (B2):** *I suggest that he **be** informed. It is essential that she **attend**.*

examples.tr: İnternet olmasaydı en iyi arkadaşımla asla tanışmazdım.

learn.turkishNote: Bu kalıpların çoğunun Türkçede de sabit karşılıkları vardır: "Ne olursa olsun" (Come what may), "Allah korusun" (Heaven forbid), "Öyle olsun" (So be it). Bu ifadeler kalıplaşmış oldukları için kelimeleri değiştirilmez: ✗ "Comes what may", ✗ "Be it that as it may". Türk öğrencilerin dikkat etmesi gereken bir nokta, "Far be it from me" ifadesinin genellikle ironik kullanıldığıdır: "Karışmak bana düşmez ama..." deyip aslında karışmak gibi.

task.prompt: Ekibinize zor bir kararı açıklayan kısa bir konuşma yapın (örneğin bir projenin ertelenmesi ya da yeni bir çalışma düzeni) (1 dakika). Were it not for / Had it not been for yapılarından birini ve en az 3 kalıplaşmış ifadeyi (Be that as it may, Come what may, Suffice it to say, Far be it from me, If need be, So be it) kullanın.
task.modelAnswer: Good morning, everyone. I'll be brief. Had it not been for the problems with our supplier, we would have launched the new product next month. Unfortunately, that is no longer possible. Suffice it to say that we've done everything we can to avoid a delay. I know many of you are disappointed, and I understand why. Be that as it may, launching a product that isn't ready would damage our reputation. Far be it from me to promise that the next few weeks will be easy, but we'll get through them. If need be, we'll bring in extra help. Come what may, we will launch in the spring.

lessons.title: Cümle çeşitliliği ve ritim
lessons.goal: Kısa ve uzun cümleleri, öne almayı, devrik yapıları ve kalıplaşmış ifadeleri bilinçli ve ölçülü kullanarak etkileyici ve ritmik bir metin yazabilirim.

discover.title: İki versiyon
discover.body:
Version A:
"The storm arrived at night. The storm was very strong. Many trees fell down. The electricity went off. People were scared. The next morning, the city was very quiet. Many streets were closed. The damage was very bad. People started to clean up."

Version B:
"The storm arrived at night. Such was its force that trees that had stood for a century were torn from the ground, and, one by one, the lights of the city went out. Nobody slept. By morning, an eerie silence had fallen over the streets. Gone were the cars, the buses, the usual morning noise. In their place lay broken branches and shattered glass. Shocked as they were, people began, slowly, to clean up."

questions.prompt: What replaced the usual morning noise?
questions.explanation: "an eerie silence had fallen over the streets"

learn.explanation:
C2 seviyesinde iyi bir yazar sadece doğru değil, **etkileyici** yazar. Bunun anahtarı **çeşitlilik** ve **ritimdir**.

**Version A neden zayıf?**

- Bütün cümleler aynı uzunlukta ve aynı yapıda (Özne + Fiil)
- Tekrar: *The storm ..., The storm ...*
- Zayıf sıfatlar: *very strong, very bad*

**Version B neden güçlü?**

| Araç | Örnek |
|---|---|
| **Kısa cümle (vurgu)** | *Nobody slept.* |
| **Uzun, akan cümle** | *Such was its force that trees ... were torn from the ground, and, one by one, ...* |
| **İleri vurgu** | *Such was its force that ...* |
| **Tamamlayıcıyı öne alma** | *Gone were the cars, ...* |
| **Yer devrikliği** | *In their place lay broken branches ...* |
| **Sıfat öne alma** | *Shocked as they were, ...* |
| **Güçlü kelimeler** | *torn, eerie, shattered* (very strong / very bad yerine) |
| **Üçleme (triplet)** | *the cars, the buses, the usual morning noise* |

**Ritim için ipuçları:**

1. **Uzun cümleden sonra kısa cümle**, vurgu yaratır.
2. Cümleleri **farklı öğelerle** başlatın: zarf, yan cümle, öne alınmış öğe.
3. **Üçlemeler** akılda kalır: *the cars, the buses, the noise*.
4. **very + sıfat** yerine güçlü tek kelimeler: *very bad → devastating*, *very quiet → silent*.

**Ölçü önemli!** Bu ünitedeki yapılar **tuz gibidir**: az kullanıldığında lezzet katar, çok kullanıldığında metni **overwrought** (abartılı, aşırı süslü) yapar. Bir paragrafta 1–2 devrik yapı genellikle yeterlidir.

examples.en: The meeting lasted six hours. Nothing was decided.
examples.tr: Toplantı altı saat sürdü. Hiçbir şeye karar verilmedi.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçe yazıda uzun ve çok yan cümleli yapılar yaygındır, bazen tek bir cümle bir paragraf kadar uzun olabilir. İngilizce yazıda ise ritim için kısa ve uzun cümleler dengeli kullanılır; özellikle bir uzun cümleden sonra gelen çok kısa bir cümle ("Nobody slept.") güçlü bir etki yaratır. Türk öğrencilerin İngilizce yazılarında görülen bir başka sorun, "very" kelimesinin aşırı kullanımıdır. C2 seviyesinde "very bad" yerine "devastating", "very tired" yerine "exhausted" gibi güçlü kelimeler tercih edilir.

task.prompt: Hayatınızı ya da bir topluluğu değiştiren bir olayı (bir doğal olay, bir taşınma, bir kayıp, büyük bir başarı) anlatan bir anı yazısı ya da köşe yazısı yazın (200–250 kelime). Uzun ve kısa cümleleri dengeli kullanın ve şu yapılardan en az 5 farklı türü ölçülü bir şekilde kullanın: öne alma (Tired as I was / Gone are the days), yer devrikliği, Such was / So + sıfat + was, olumsuz devrik (Not once / Nowhere / Only then), Had it not been for, kalıplaşmış ifade (Be that as it may / Come what may / Suffice it to say). very + sıfat kullanmayın.
task.modelAnswer:
The Summer the River Rose

I was twelve when the river burst its banks. It had been raining for nine days. On the tenth, the water came.

Such was its speed that within an hour, the ground floor of our house had disappeared. My father carried my little brother on his shoulders; my mother held my hand so tightly that it hurt. Not once did she let go. We spent the night on the roof of the school, along with half the village, wrapped in blankets and watching the dark water rise.

By morning, the rain had stopped. Gone were the gardens, the market stalls, the small wooden bridge where we used to fish. In their place lay mud, broken furniture and an extraordinary, unbearable silence.

Had it not been for our neighbours, I am not sure how we would have survived the weeks that followed. Exhausted as they were, they shared food, dried each other's clothes and rebuilt each other's walls. Only then did I understand what the word "community" really meant.

Suffice it to say that the village was never quite the same. Nowhere else have I seen people so devastated and yet so generous. Thirty years later, the river is calm. I am not. Every time it rains for more than a day, I remember the roof, the blankets, and my mother's hand.

questions.modelAnswer:
The Street Where I Grew Up

When I was a child, our street was the whole world. At one end stood the bakery, where Mr Yücel sold warm simit at six every morning. At the other was the small mosque, its courtyard full of pigeons and old men playing backgammon.

Such was the sense of community that nobody locked their doors. Not once do I remember feeling unsafe. Children played football until the street lights came on, and every adult was, in a sense, everyone's parent.

Then, slowly, things changed. Gone are the bakery, the tailor and the little shop that sold everything from batteries to rose water. In their place stand glass towers, a car park and a chain coffee shop. Modern as the new buildings are, they have no character. Few of the families I knew still live there.

Far be it from me to romanticise the past. Life was not always easy, and many of the old houses were cold and damp. Be that as it may, something important has been lost. Were it not for a handful of residents who still meet every Friday in the mosque courtyard, the street would have no memory at all.

I went back last month. The pigeons were still there. So, remarkably, was one of the old men, still playing backgammon. He recognised me at once. Only then did I realise how much I had missed it.
